a.text: A land of freedom, happiness and order, one of the few left in this chaotic world.
Have you ever known doubt, my child?
How was our city built, how did it grow, and how did it prosper?
Why is there only one Laterano? Why is it called the eternal paradise?
If the fires of war burn once more, and peace falls into ruin before our eyes—
Will the world continue to tolerate Paradise?

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: They are here, Your Holiness.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: Are you sure about this? There is no precedent for it, aside from the canonization of the popes. It's risky.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: You are correct. I could find no such record in our millennium of history.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: But that is of no concern.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: What is of concern is the warning I received.

spans.text: of concern is the warning I received.

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: What is it about, specifically?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I would answer your question honestly, if I could.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Our glowing faith has warned us that danger is near. But no one knows what it is, or how it will arrive.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I only see a list of names.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: First on the list is the main character of today's performance.

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: That's why you proposed canonizing him?

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: Still the title of 'Saint' is special, reserved for the holy ones who built Laterano.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I hold the same title.

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: Th-That's different! You're the Pope, sir.

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: You're conceding a significant amount of power. He will have the right to participate in a multitude of matters, even policy-making... this is no small thing!

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Easy, Giovanni. Nothing ventured, nothing gained.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: And, as I said, there is more than one name on the list.

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: What? Are you proposing that all of them be canonized?!

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: That's absu—I mean, against the rules!

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Don't be so quick to judge, Giovanni. We need to find them first.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I saw some familiar names. Do you know who's on it?

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: No idea.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: In that case, I'll let it remain a secret for a little longer.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Giovanni.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I think I'll visit these friends after the ceremony.

steps.name: Joyous Lateran
steps.text: Why are there so many balloons?

steps.name: Joyous Lateran
steps.text: There's even a pie throwing competition on that street up ahead. I had to take a detour because of all the pies on the ground... is there some sort of festival on?

steps.name: Spirited Lateran
steps.text: No idea. Heard it's a ceremony or something, but I don't know the specifics.

steps.name: Spirited Lateran
steps.text: Who cares, at the end of the day? Let's just enjoy the occasion, like we always do.

steps.name: Spirited Lateran
steps.text: Say, do you think I could fly if I tied myself to these balloons?

steps.name: Joyous Lateran
steps.text: You don't have a prayer, even if you lost twenty pounds.

steps.name: Spirited Lateran
steps.text: Don't say that! Maybe I could take off my jacket. It's a pretty warm day...

steps.name: Spirited Lateran
steps.text: Hey, look, new balloons!

steps.name: Spirited Lateran
steps.text: Here, hold my jacket, I've got to try this!

steps.name: Joyous Lateran
steps.text: Hey! Be careful!

steps.name: Spirited Lateran
steps.text: Whoooooooa! I'm flying!

steps.name: Spirited Lateran
steps.text: Hey, how do I stop climbing?

steps.name: Spirited Lateran
steps.text: Oh no! I forgot I'm scared of heights!
Pardon.

steps.name: Joyous Lateran
steps.text: Hey! Don't go! Help!
Hm?

steps.name: Spirited Lateran
steps.text: Help! Let me down!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Spirited Lateran
steps.text: Ouch!

steps.name: Spirited Lateran
steps.text: Man, that hurt... but thanks.

steps.name: Spirited Lateran
steps.text: My balloons...

steps.name: Spirited Lateran
steps.text: You popped them all? Did you really have to be so cruel?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It was the logical solution, given the circumstances.

steps.name: Spirited Lateran
steps.text: I guess... but couldn't you have left me a couple?

steps.name: Joyous Lateran
steps.text: He got you down, stop whining. Don't mind this idiot, sir.

steps.name: Joyous Lateran
steps.text: Where did you get that outfit? It looks cool.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I can't say.

steps.name: Joyous Lateran
steps.text: What do you mean? Was it a gift?

steps.name: Spirited Lateran
steps.text: Looks like a work uniform. There's something familiar about it...

steps.name: Joyous Lateran
steps.text: Where do you get a uniform like that? I'm applying!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...I'm not sure it's a standard uniform.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You can submit your curriculum vitae to the Curia.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: '....They led the Sankta. They built a city and named it Laterano.'

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: 'And when disaster looms once more, a new revelation shall dawn upon the Sankta, and a new guide shall lead forth...'

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: 'The Paradise of the Sankta shall remain eternal, as witnessed by the world.'

steps.name: Legatus
steps.text: We bear witness.

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: We bear witness.

steps.name: Cleric
steps.text: We bear witness.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Ite, missa est.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: You can raise your head now, my child.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: No... a different name is appropriate here.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Raise your head and stand by my side, Saint Federico Giallo, the first Chosen of Laterano who does not come from the ranks of the popes.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: A measured reaction. Not a fan of the balloons?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I don't understand.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: What is the duty of a Saint? What is the disaster that looms? Does it call for immediate action?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I need to know the details in order to formulate a plan.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: An appropriate question, but not one I am able to answer.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The warning I received was as cryptic as it was direct. It does not provide for a specific answer.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Each era has its own trials and tribulations, for which we can only prepare to the best of our ability. It is certain, however, that you have been chosen because It believes that you have the ability to respond to the unknown.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...I don't understand.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: There is no hurry. We have time.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Right now, there are other things we can talk about... this garb suits you, Federico.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Makes all the cardinals' bickering over the cut and color worthwhile.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I didn't think that was a cardinal's duty.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Let's not be so strict. People can't help but focus on that which draws their interest.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I've seen your resume, Federico. I can tell that you are an outstanding executor.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The Commandments do not bind your thoughts as they do others, eh?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Rules can be broken, if necessary.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Of course. I can't bring myself to disagree.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: You judge matters by your own standards. That is why you always carry out your missions effectively, if somewhat unorthodoxly.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I have a mission for you. I had intended on going myself, but there are other matters that require my attention... now, I've found someone who can go in my stead.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: It will not be an easy task. Expect unexpected complications, the likes of which you have never seen.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: But I believe you are up to it. I want to see why He chose you.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Will you go, Federico?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Executor Federico, ready for assignment.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: What is your command?

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: What are you looking at, Arturia?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The flowers, Excellency.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: This is the only place in the monastery where they grow. I'm glad I made it in time for bloom season. It's a view worth savoring.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: Clément would be happy to hear it.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: It has been a long time since anyone came to see the flowers that he cared for. They used to grow all around the abbey.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: This is all that is left.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: A shame. I understand there is a beautiful story behind them.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: There was.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: What about now?

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: Perhaps there still is. But my eyes have grown weak. Flowers are no longer pure enjoyment for me. I've grown too old, spent too much time here.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: Flowers cannot fill an empty stomach, just as your music can soothe pain but not avert aging.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: I know things don't always go according to plan. Perhaps this was inevitable the moment our call for help reached Laterano.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: Now...

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: Only the bitter fruit remains.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Bitter fruit. Even the name itself leaves a bitterness on the tip of the tongue that does not go away. I rather like it, actually.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Poor soil does not bear sweet fruit.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: Poor soil. Yes, poor soil.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: But it's home for people like us.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: I thought we would find a better, more peaceful life.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: We had walls that protected us from wind and rain, we had faith unwavering. Our longing for a peaceful life won out over our longing for home.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: All that was left was to find a quiet corner of the world where we could live in peace.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: But now...
The old man's emaciated face twitches slightly.
It is as though he is mustering the strength to tear apart that which threatens to crush him beneath his loose skin. His words are replaced by a string of coughs and gasps.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: How many years has it been? Fifty? Sixty? More?

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: When disaster came from the sea, when we rejected the Inquisition's demands and left Iberia to settle here... I've seen children born, and then buried those same children.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: Life has become hard.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Life is always hard.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: Yes, you're right...

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: Look at the living. To where do they belong? I can't tell.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: Are they of Iberia, or of Laterano?

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: We've come too far in too long...

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: Arturia.

steps.name: Gaunt Old Man
steps.text: Am I still a Lateran, after all these years?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Only you know the answer, Abbot Stefano Torregrossa.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I hope I still am.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Then you are.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: You spoke the truth, Arturia.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: There's no need to test me anymore.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: A misunderstanding. I never intended to probe your secrets.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I permitted you to stay because these doors are open to all who bear no ill intentions.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: But I still don't know what you are seeking, Arturia.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: What if I said I seek nothing?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I take it you don't believe it.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Then let me put it this way. Pay no heed to me. I promise I will not interfere with anything here, nor with your decisions.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I'm simply a traveler, drawn to this place by the stories here, praying that the ending is a good one.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Should I swear in the name of my halo?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: You're a cunning one, Arturia.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: But I believe your words.
The old man falls silent again.
Do all who grow old grow dry and stiff? The lines on his face, once so beloved, now cast only lethargy.
The eyes have become clouded by the decades that they have seen.
The face should have been warmer, gentler, more Lateran.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: The Holy City never answered, all these years, but I never stopped praying.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: My faith taught me to love, to be kind. It did not teach me to abandon our brothers and sisters, our loyal friends.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: To abandon the few for the happiness of the many...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The devoted would call it a shameful betrayal.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Do you?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I don't have that answer, Arturia.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Where does the believer go, if faith has betrayed itself?

steps.name: Weathered Hunter
steps.text: Here's the stuff.

steps.name: Weathered Hunter
steps.text: Get it salted and dried quickly. It should last the winter.

steps.name: Gaunt Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: I'll get someone on it!

steps.name: Gaunt Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Gratias. This meat will buy us some time...

steps.name: Weathered Hunter
steps.text: ...I'm sorry.

steps.name: Weathered Hunter
steps.text: Finding game was harder than I thought, with the weather is getting colder.

steps.name: Gaunt Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Don't say that!

steps.name: Gaunt Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Thanks to you, there will be meat on the table for the children tonight... don't apologize.

steps.name: Weathered Hunter
steps.text: Ha. Okay, forget what I said. Make them something good for dinner.

steps.name: Gaunt Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: I would love to, but we've got to ration.

steps.name: Gaunt Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Where's Hyman? She didn't get hurt, did she?

steps.name: Weathered Hunter
steps.text: Don't worry, she's fine.

steps.name: Gaunt Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Really?

steps.name: Gaunt Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Don't hide anything, okay? An injury is no small thing.

steps.name: Weathered Hunter
steps.text: No problem, we'll come back if we do need anything.

steps.name: Weathered Hunter
steps.text: It's getting late. I should go.

steps.name: Gaunt Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Hey, Gerald!

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Gaunt Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Everyone's been talking about Laterano. They mean no harm; they're just a little anxious.

steps.name: Gaunt Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Please, don't mind it if someone lets something slip.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Gaunt Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: I-I see, that's good... yes...

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Thanks for coming, Raimund.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Let's go. We're not needed here. Is Hyman back yet?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Haven't seen her all day. Davy led a group out to look for her. I'll join them later.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: We have a scout team ready. We'll have concrete intel when they get back tonight.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Good. Carry on.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Brother Gerald...

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Are we really going to accept things as they are right now?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Calm down, Raimund.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: You know we never had of a choice.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: So we're compromising?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: What are we? What have all these years been for? What's the difference between us and them? We're just—

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Raimund!

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: That's enough.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: But—

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: No buts.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I know you don't like it, Raimund.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: There's still time. If there's someone you want to see, go and see them.

a.text: Ingestion of food for the organism's survival.
It is the basis of life, and the fundamental instinct of all animals.
Activities for the sake of survival.
The most legitimate desire there is.

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: I wanted to try to persuade you, but now is not really the time.

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: You're weak. Too many things interfere with our thoughts, warp our judgment, preventing us from following the guidance of our faith.

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: You can no longer hear me, can you?
There is no answer.
The priest's voice mixes with a strange sound, echoing through the underground space.
The sound of eating.
The sound of ripping food apart and swallowing it.
Life that has lost its original form grows in the shadows.

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: It's almost winter. The sun has become a rare sight.

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: This building is like a remote island. It has held out long enough. It can no longer hold out.

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: See the gaps in the walls, where the draught comes through.

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: There is little fuel left. Many will suffer in the cold without winter supplies.

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: Of course, we're not entirely helpless.

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: There are a couple of small Originium veins nearby, aren't there?

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: Originium can be mined there for energy generation, as you have done for many years.

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: But it's dangerous. Everyone knows the risk of Oripathy infection.

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: Who would take such a risk if they had a choice? Oripathy is a death sentence on an island like this.

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: You left your homes and came here. You accepted the most dangerous jobs in order to find a place to call your new home.

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: You're an indispensable part of this abbey.

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: You still can't hear me, can you?

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: I must admit...

steps.name: Gentle Priest
steps.text: I feel a little sad.

steps.name: Sankta Girl
steps.text: Hello? Anyone? Any—

steps.name: Sankta Girl
steps.text: Whoa!

steps.name: Sankta Girl
steps.text: What's with all the broken glass?

steps.name: Gaunt Man
steps.text: Fortuna? Good timing.

steps.name: Gaunt Man
steps.text: Give me a hand with this window frame, will you? The wind broke the window. I'm trying to plug it up.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: No problem!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Didn't we fix this a couple of days ago? I remember my teeth chattering in the cold while listening to Father Stefano's sermon.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Should I get some tape?

steps.name: Gaunt Man
steps.text: I'm afraid tape won't do. The pieces are all over the place, and I don't think I can put it back. Sorry...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Why apologize to me, Patruus Clément? It's not your fault.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: What should we do? Find something to block it up. The wind's rather cold... should I find some unused fabric?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Don't waste it, save it for clothes. It's getting cold.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: There should be some planks left from when Gerald took those old houses apart. I'll go look for them.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: That will do it for the frame. Thanks, Fortuna.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: What were you here for anyway?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Oh! I wanted to see if there's anything to eat because I missed lunch. It's all Fina's fault...

steps.name: Solemn Girl
steps.text: What's my fault?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Fina!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: What are you doing here?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Listening to you talk behind my back.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I'm just telling it like it is! That wouldn't have taken so long if you didn't keep going on and on about it.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: It's because you were dumb enough to get scammed!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I told you to be careful of Lemuen! She's been talking to everyone, pretending to care. Who knows what she's really after?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: You've been absent-minded lately. Did she say something to you?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: No! No one said anything to me! I'm not being absent-minded!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Yes, you are.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: We're all Sankta, Tuna. You can't fool me.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: So is Lemuen. You know she has no ill intentions. Why won't you trust her?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Why do you hate people from Laterano so much? We were Laterans too, weren't we?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Father Stefano says we can go back soon. Why did we lock up the Lateran emissaries?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Why don't we go back?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Because Raimund and the others can't go with us! Isn't that reason enough?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: You want to leave them behind? Well, I don't!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: That's not what I mean!

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Then what do you mean?!

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Enough!

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: The Abbot has his reasons. Say no more.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I'll find some planks to board up the window... you two calm down.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Can't you sense my thoughts, Fina?

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I can, Tuna.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: But I...

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: Never mind. I lost my cool. I know that wasn't what you meant.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I was wrong too.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: You always have that gun with you. You got it from your dad, right? I thought it didn't work anymore.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: It doesn't. Maybe it's a parts problem. And I don't know how to use a gun myself...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: But I'm not carrying it to use it anyway.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I always thought it was a decorative accessory.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Partly.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Holding the gun like this is like praying.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: That's what Dad said when he gave it to me. He said it was a Sankta practice.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: I don't know about any practices like that.

steps.name: Delfina
steps.text: My grandma's gun is in a canyon.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: We can share, Fina.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I'll try to get it fixed, then we can use it together.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Now, let us pray.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: The planks should be here somewhere...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Aha. There.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: That should be enough. I could fix the outside windows too, if there are any leftover.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: And fuel...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Not much fuel left. *sigh*

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Who goes there?!

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: ...No one?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Am I seeing things?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: The terrain is so strange. Do you still call this a desert? There's a canyon below?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Mind your step.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: I never knew you were such a gentleman, Richele.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Nothing good ever happens comes from you complimenting me...

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Don't be so uptight. Your bank account is safe this time.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Is that the nomadic abbey we're looking for?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I think so.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: What do we do? Knock on the front door?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: You think someone will answer?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: What do you think, Federico?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Approach.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Roger. Er, should we do a quick briefing first?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Target building has been identified. It is a large mobile complex built jointly by Iberia and Laterano in 1011, official name Sanctilaminium Ambrosii.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Originally controlled by Iberia, it disappeared after straying from its route 61 years ago.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Laterano received a request for help from the abbey one month ago and sent two nuncios to investigate.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Straightforward enough up to this point.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: So how did we end up losing contact with our nuncios and bringing in big guns like you two?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: My mission is to discover the whereabouts of Cardinal Aide Lemuen and Legatus Oren Argiolas, and to guarantee their safety.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am also to ensure that the abbey is able to function normally and avoid casualties.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: So His Holiness wants you take it easy?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Well, I signed up for Lemuen. I couldn't care less what happens to Oren.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Your personal feelings are irrelevant.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Target status is unclear, and we are unable to determine if the inhabitants of the building are hostile.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: What do we do, then? Infiltrate and investigate?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I suggest we take the most direct path and finish this quickly.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If they are deceased, I will return their bones to Laterano.
